sentences.text:
Shri R.B.
Tiwari - Advocate for appellant.
Shri S.P. Chadhar - Public Prosecutor for State.
Heard on I.A. No.28718 of 2025 which is a third application under Section 430(1) of BNSS, 2023 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

His first application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 15.10.2025 and his second application for temporary suspension of sentence was allowed vide order dated 20.11.2025.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 29.08.2025 passed by the learned First Additional Sessions Judge, Chhatarpur (M.P.) in Sessions Trial No.1300097 of 2015, whereby the appellant has been convicted under Sections 419/120-B, 420/120-B, 467/120-B and 471/120-B of the IPC and sentence to undergo R.I. for 03 years and fine of Rs.5,000/-, R.I. for 03 years and fine of Rs.5,000/-, R.I. for 05 years and fine of Rs.10,000/- and R.I. for 05 years and fine of Rs.10,000/-
respectively, with default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the learned trial Court has wrongly convicted the present appellant without proper appreciation of facts of the case.

It is contended that, as per the prosecution case, the present appellant along with other co-accused persons is alleged to have committed fraud and forgery with the complainant Mukesh Soni (PW-1) and to have 2 CRA-8718-2025 entered into an agreement for sale of land to the tune of Rs.50 lakhs, out of which Rs.5 lakhs is alleged to have been misappropriated.
It is further alleged that a total sum of Rs.20 lakhs was obtained and utilized by the present appellant along with the co-accused persons on the basis of the said agreement.

Learned counsel further submits that the deposition of Mukesh Soni (PW-1), particularly paragraph 24 thereof, reveals that no agreement was executed by the present appellant nor was any agreement seized in his name thereby indicating that the appellant was not a party to the alleged transaction and was merely a witness to the agreement.

It is further submitted that the appellant remained in custody during the course of trial from 29.08.2025 to 22.11.2025 and subsequent to his conviction, he has been in continuous custody since 01.12.2025.
He is ready and willing to comply with any conditions that may be imposed by this Court.
It is also contended that the present appeal is not likely to be heard in the near future and is likely to take considerable time for final disposal.

Therefore, having regard to the period of custody already undergone, it is prayed that the benefit of suspension of sentence be granted and the appellant be released on bail during Gya Prasad Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73957304/
1 the pendency of the appeal.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer made by the appellant, submitting that complainant Mukesh Soni (PW-1) has categorically levelled allegations against the present appellant and that the appellant was actively involved in the commission of the offence.

sentences.text: It is further contended that the mere absence of any agreement in the name of the appellant does not, by itself, discredit or 3 CRA-8718-2025 belie the prosecution case.

In view of the aforesaid,
no case for suspension of sentence and grant of bail is made out.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties at length and upon due consideration of the material available on record, particularly in light of the categorical allegations levelled by the complainant,
Mukesh Soni (PW-1), indicating the appellant's active involvement in the commission of the offence,
this Court is of the considered opinion that no case for suspension of sentence is made out.

Further, having regard to the nature and gravity of the offences, the manner in which they are alleged to have been committed, and the overall facts and circumstances of the case, this Court finds that the appellant has failed to make out a case warranting grant of bail.

At this stage, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court finds no sufficient ground to grant the benefit of suspension of sentence and release the appellant on bail during the pendency of the appeal.
Accordingly, I.A. No.28718 of 2025, being devoid of merit, is hereby rejected.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE THK Gya Prasad Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73957304/
